Author: @queengeekrose9467
Content: Guys, one thing you may not realize about WHY Tammy was probably so toxic when she was so heavy was how much pain she was in all the time.  Pain can make people cope in very bad ways and make them lash out, especially at people who are trying to help them - and if the person who is in pain has been bullied, which let's face, a person who has been overweight that badly their whole life almost HAD to have been bullied for it somewhat along the way, they will have less than stellar coping skills to begin with and be angry about a lot of things, making the dealing with the pain even harder - and if they are angry about being overweight, and anyone mentions it, they will not be receptive to hearing about that and just lash out about that, thinking they are about to get bullied or abused, most likely.  It's a bad cycle, and a very hard one to break, especially since the overweight person is likely facing a lot of difficulty moving and other health issues involving mobility.   As someone who has a number of health issues myself, I understand this all too well (mine are autoimmune - multiple conditions, including one similar to MS - and a SEVERELY damaged spine from a car accident, which have left me in a wheelchair, almost completely unable to walk) and know how limiting my exercise options are.  If I move wrong, I could literally snap my spinal cord or break bones / tear ligaments because of my conditions.  I have to be extremely cautious.  I still need to exercise, don't get me wrong, I just have to be extra cautious.  As Tammy lost weight, a lot of her pain probably was reduced - the weight was probably causing her pain and literally crushing her - and she had to go through physical therapy as she was losing weight anyway, as part of the process, to relearn to walk, or walk better, and to take care of herself more.  As she went, pain management is part of that process to, and in general, I would bet, that is a large part of what helped her attitude shift to a lot more positive - along with the therapy she was / is getting as part of the whole process.  She has made wonderful progress towards becoming a happier, healthier person in general, and it's sad to see Amy slipping backwards so much, even as Tammy is making such forward progress.
